subject: Private Offer: buyer risk profiles and term optimization options
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finovate.io>

Cc: procurement@finovate.io
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer term length and approval routing questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Finovate is trying to align on how to structure the AWS private offer so it fits both our capital cadence and internal risk thresholds. Two quick asks:

1) Would Redwood consider a 24-month private offer with a quarterly usage true-up (vs a standard 12-month)? Finance is pushing longer terms but we need flexibility on variable consumption.
2) What buyer-level approvals typically trigger legal + finance review on your side? Our SOWs sometimes exceed $250k ARR, and different approvers are needed depending on committed spend.

Attaching our internal buyer risk summary for context. Looking for a short decision by Friday so we can keep the supplier review on schedule.

Cheers,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement | Finovate Inc.
procurement@finovate.io

Attachments: Buyer_Risk_Matrix.pdf (pdf)

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer term length and approval routing questions

Hi Samantha — really appreciate the clear asks and the risk matrix. Short answers up front: we can do a 24-month private offer with quarterly usage true-ups, and buyer approval routing depends on committed ARR + payment terms. Details below.

Options we typically present (trade-offs summarized):
- 12m term, pay-as-you-go (no commit): easiest to approve internally, higher unit price, minimal legal review.
- 12m term, annual commit (prepaid): requires procurement + finance signoff if >$100k; legal review for any custom terms.
- 24m term, committed minimum + quarterly true-up: attractive unit pricing, Finance sign-off required if committed ARR >$250k; Legal tightens auto-renew/termination clauses.
- 36m enterprise lock (with annual performance SLA): deep discounting; requires VP-level procurement and Legal + Security signoff.

For Finovate specifically, if your committed ARR remains below $300k and payment is Net-60 with quarterly true-ups, we can route through our standard private offer flow (Seller console -> Marketplace PO -> finance approval). If you are targeting >$500k commit or want extended payment terms (Net-90/Net-120), we treat that as a flagged exception that needs leadership approval (Sales leadership + Revenue Ops).

Notes on buyer risk profiles and gating:
- Low-risk buyers (existing enterprise customers with active MSA): self-service private offer, minimal gating.
- Moderate-risk (new buyer with references): need procurement + finance review; discount tiers apply.
- High-risk (startups with limited track record or complex compliance needs): involve legal and security early; consider shorter initial term + renewal option.

I’ve attached a short term-scenario worksheet and a sample private-offer template. Vanessa / Vivek — can you confirm our approval thresholds and any co-sell incentive that should be reflected for Finovate?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachments: PO_Term_Scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_PrivateOffer_Term_Summary.docx (docx)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer term length and approval routing questions

Thanks Grace — correct on most points. A few clarifications from the seller/marketplace side:

1) Approval thresholds (current internal guidance):
   - <$100k commit: Sales + AM signoff only (auto-approve in seller console).
   - $100k–$300k: Sales + Finance review; Marketplace PO created after Finance ok.
   - $300k–$750k: Sales + Finance + Legal (light review).
   - >$750k: Executive escalation (VP Sales + Legal + Revenue Ops) and security/compliance vetting.

2) Term structure recommendation for Finovate: 24-month commit with quarterly true-ups is reasonable if Finovate agrees to Net-60 and a modest overage protection (we cap quarterly price increases). If Finovate needs Net-90 we should add an early-payment discount to offset risk.

3) Co-sell considerations: if the AWS co-sell motion is material (account team will engage APN), we can layer a co-sell uplift that keeps the private offer price competitive while preserving margin for co-sell credits. Let us know if you want to route this through our APN co-sell queue.

Karthik — confirm the signature window we should include in the PO template for 24m deals (how long we hold pricing).

-Vanessa

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Marketplace & Channel | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer term length and approval routing questions

Agree with Vanessa. Operational notes for the 24-month with quarterly true-up:
- Price hold: 30 days from draft PO creation.
- Billing cadence: Quarterly invoicing with Net-60 terms default; Net-90 can be allowed but needs Revenue Ops approval.
- Auto-renew: we prefer an opt-in renewal for multi-year POs; auto-renewal creates additional legal exposure.
- Approvals in HubSpot: flag deal stage "PO - Marketplace" and set custom property "PO_commit_amount" so Finance is alerted automatically for >$100k.

I’ll update the template (linked in drive) with the signature window and approval checklist. Grace — can you share the Finovate buyer risk matrix we received so I can map approvals to their profiles?

-Karthik

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finovate.io>

- 24-month private offer with quarterly usage true-up.
- Commit: $275,000 first-year minimum; year 2 subject to quarterly true-ups.
- Payment: Net-60.
- Signature window: 21 days from PO issuance.

We accept the 30-day price hold you suggested and will route for internal finance approval this afternoon. Attached is our formal purchase intent and a filled risk matrix. If Finance signs off, we’ll expect a Marketplace PO link and a draft private-offer for signature.

Appreciate the speed — Samantha
